P1.evidence: The title carries a KFS suffix but belongs to a different prospect, and no setter is named or implied anywhere on the call, so the read-back check cannot be fairly assessed. The standard two-part frame ran — 'where are you today? Where do you want to be? We can help. I can show you one of the many options that we have. Okay?' — with 'what's in the way' and 'what you need' missing. Open question ran, though it had to be repeated twice because of the connection.

P2.evidence: P2b is the one clean hit — 'What do you do for work?' produced the forklift role and the rep followed it into the manual lifting, which mattered. Age was asked and then apparently not absorbed, since the rep twice afterwards described him as entering his forties having heard '59 this year'. Height and weight never asked. P2d is the costly partial: the injury was volunteered in the first answer, the rep asked 'When was this?' and established the timeline, and then stopped — no question about what the injury is, whether anyone has assessed it, what movements are contraindicated, or whether it is improving. That a year-old injury blocks bench press and curls came out only because the prospect said so. Diet, sleep and energy were never touched.

P3.evidence: The physical ladder was the best work on the call. Three consecutive 'Why?' questions — genuinely just 'Why?', twice — drove past the surface to 'I want to have a body capable of doing whatever I want. I want to go to the mountain and be walking more than one or two hours without getting tired. I want to do moves with no pain', and then to the dogs, Airsoft and the boxes at work. He also pushed twice into the emotional impact ('has this had an impact on you mentally?') and got the loss of fulfilment. But the relational half never ran at all: P3f and P3g were skipped entirely, so a man of 59 was never asked about a partner, children, grandchildren, legacy or identity. There is no ripple frame in this call beyond his own body.

P4.evidence: P4f ran and ran well — 'what's the rationale in terms of getting outside help as opposed to doing this yourself?' — and the prospect named the gap himself in the answer: 'maybe if I was with a coach in the strength workout, maybe I will not be hurt in my body.' The rep then asked what he needed from a coach and got structure, technique correction and progression, which is a clean P4e. Past attempts and the reason they stopped were established mostly through the injury timeline rather than by asking.

P5.evidence: Credit where due: the rep asked the why-now question three separate times and refused to accept the first two deflections — 'I understand you've probably seen us recently, but I'm really wondering, what was the moment where you said to yourself internally, enough is enough?' That persistence produced the consequence in the prospect's own words: 'it's now, or maybe I will stop working out and be the same man I was two years ago, only sitting on the sofa. And doing nothing. Getting a big, big fat belly.' The settle check, the why-not and the line in the sand never ran, and the honest read of the three attempts is that the prospect never really had a trigger event — which was itself a signal worth acting on.

P6.evidence: The 1-10 check returned a five or six and the rep handled that well — he refused to move on, twice — 'a five or six tells me you have some questions or thoughts or concerns or queries' and 'a five or six, man, it tells me that there are some things that you're not so confident about' — which surfaced that the hesitation was money rather than belief. He then isolated correctly and got a strong confidence answer: 'If I make a decision, if I go all in, I know it will work.' P6a's actual question never ran and P6b missed again.

P11.evidence: Nothing was sold. Both coaching tiers were declined on affordability and the $200 product was deferred to mid-June, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The isolate ran, and early — 'Don't worry about that for now. I just want to make sure that you're confident in the plan... Because the main thing is helping you' — which correctly separated belief from budget and produced 'I'm super confident with your plan.' Then nothing. He never came back for the financial picture: no permission question, no cash on hand, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. The only money questions asked were 'Is the reason because of finances or is there any other reason?' and 'When would you feel like you'd be in a position to do this?' The same rep ran the complete sequence on the Cole Carson call the same day, so this is a lapse rather than an inability. He also primed the objection before the pitch with an unscripted challenge — 'it's not a free lunch at the end of the day... are you ultimately prepared to invest a significant amount into yourself?' — which invited the money conversation eight minutes before the offer.

Triggered plainly — 'This month, I cannot. I have to wait the next maybe.' Not one OD move ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. The rep accepted it, dated a callback for mid-June and released him to free content. Arguably the humane call given the disclosed financial position, but scored against the script it is a miss.

The clinical gap. A year-old unresolved elbow and shoulder injury that prevents pressing, curling and lifting at work was raised in the prospect's opening sentence and there is no scripted gate requiring the rep to establish what it is or whether it has been assessed before recommending loaded work. Worse than passive here: the rep went on to give specific unsupervised loading advice ('I'd stick to the 6 if 12 is a bit uncomfortable') and to send him to free online content to 'alleviate some of these problems in your body'. Process defect, but the free-content advice is the rep's own addition.

notes: The 'Why?' laddering in Phase 3 is the best example of that technique in the batch and produced concrete, usable goals from a prospect who struggled in English. Three things to fix. The relational half of Phase 3 never ran, so a 59-year-old was never asked who else this affects — the single biggest missed lever on this call. The financial picture was isolated and then abandoned, unlike the same rep's work on Cole Carson the same day. And the injury that is the entire reason for the call was given one question about timing and no others, before the rep prescribed a kettlebell weight and pointed him at Instagram.
